properties.metisTriageReason: Verdict: The finding is valid because the hash-compare path forwards in_vec[1] and in_vec[2] bases and lengths directly to psa_hash_compare without local validation. Evidence: tfm_crypto_hash_interface copies input/hash pointers and lengths from in_vec[1]/in_vec[2] at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_hash.c:130, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_hash.c:131, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_hash.c:132, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_hash.c:133 and immediately calls psa_hash_compare at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_hash.c:135; the dispatcher only validates in_vec[0].len before dispatching hash requests at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_init.c:209 and secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_init.c:236. Gap: none.
properties.mitigation: Add explicit validation before forwarding buffers: check that each base is non-NULL when its length is nonzero, and reject malformed vectors with PSA_ERROR_PROGRAMMER_ERROR. Consider validating hash_length against the expected digest length for iov->alg where appropriate.
properties.reasoning: The hash compare path reads vector metadata for in_vec[1] and in_vec[2] and forwards their bases and lengths to psa_hash_compare without local validation that the bases are non-NULL for nonzero lengths or that the hash buffer is present. Because this function is an API shim receiving PSA vectors, malformed caller-controlled vectors may be able to trigger secure-side faults or out-of-bounds reads in lower layers if validation is not uniformly performed elsewhere. The reviewed file provides no evidence of such earlier checks.
